facts.raw_span: A 9-year-old boy presented with a swelling on the right anterior chest
the swelling had first appeared as a pea-sized nodule three years earlier
the lesion had gradually increased to approximately 0.5 cm in diameter
the mass was lobulated, smooth-surfaced, bony hard, fixed to the underlying rib, and non-tender
the overlying skin was normal and freely mobile
A tangential chest radiograph showed a bony outgrowth arising from the lateral aspect of the right sixth rib
He had no pain, tenderness, or respiratory symptoms
no other swellings
Osteochondroma was suspected
